analysis:
Examined all supplied BASE excerpts of provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift (lines 1–1116) and the bounded patch. The changes expand autopilot history with detail (HEAD 342–343) and introduce placement adoption, holds, busy continuity, watchdog cancellation and startup-stop state (HEAD 355 onward). Stored state alone does not establish a security regression; its mutation and enforcement paths are not supplied, and the patch is truncated.
Relevant contracts are inference availability/cancellation and native ownership (TB-007, T-010, T-029), model identity and placement integrity (T-007, T-012, T-027), connection-bound authorization (TB-011, T-053), and encrypted scoped cache reuse (T-041). BASE retains per-process X25519 generation (833), advertised-model eligibility filtering (814–830), configured slot caps (308–310), fleet KV budgeting (856–859), cancellation tracking (535), and separate artifact/cache identities (932–934). No shown change alters encryption, attestation, credential handling, fan authority or billing; this is not verification of their external implementations.
Integration should examine ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement and watchdog/startup-preload consumers: holds must not override hard memory caps or lifecycle drains; adopted inventory models must retain eligibility, load-bound hash/cache bindings and coordinator placement authority; stalled operations completing after cancellation must preserve native ownership and cannot publish a lease or placement. Check history-detail producers for prompt or credential exposure. These are unresolved implementation contracts, not demonstrated missing controls. HEAD implementations and remaining added state are needed to resolve these PR-specific availability and placement questions.
